premise: I poured my $112,000 403(b) into a handcrafted wooden rocking‑horse workshop with my daughter, notarizing a 50/50 partnership and a promise of a free horse for each grandchild, but when a toy‑museum chain bid $460,000 for the brand and patterns she forged a dissolution, sold everything, and mailed me a $3,200 ‘rocking’ check; I found our original contract hidden under the saddle of a finished horse, proved the forgery, and now run ‘Gallop of Deceit Rocking Horses,’ where she sands manes in a smock that says ‘Unbridled Lies’ and every hoof stamp prints the perjury case number.
